sections.history: Tirupayathangudi, whose Tevaram name is Tiruppayatrur, lies near Tiruvarur (about 14–15 km, by way of Surakkudi) in Nagapattinam district, set between the Arasilar and Vettaru rivers and some 15 km from the coast. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirunavukkarasar (Appar). The stone temple belongs to the Chola period and later, standing over the far older sacred site the saint had already made famous.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Payatrunathar in the sanctum, with the goddess Kaviyangkanni Ammai — also called Nethrambigai, 'the goddess of the eye' — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The sacred tank is the Karuna Theertham, 'the tank of grace,' whose waters are central to the healing tradition of the place.
sections.legends: The temple is above all a place of healing for the eyes. Devotees who suffer from diseases of the eye come to bathe in the Karuna Theertham and to worship Nethrambigai, whose very name joins the goddess to the eye (netra), and her lord Payatrunathar; by this grace relief is sought and, by long tradition, found. The fuller sthala purana, like those of many smaller delta shrines, is preserved chiefly in local memory and the Tevaram verses of Appar.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Devotees seeking relief from eye ailments visit through the year, and pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail near Tiruvarur include Tirupayathangudi among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tirupayathangudi the pilgrim comes to a shrine of gentle, specific grace — the lord and goddess who heal the eyes. Before Payatrunathar and Nethrambigai, beside the Karuna Theertham, the visitor feels the tender compassion of a delta temple to which the troubled have long come for sight and solace, carrying the hope of the goddess of the eye.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tirupayathangudi is near Tiruvarur (about 14–15 km, via Surakkudi), between the Arasilar and Vettaru rivers, in Nagapattinam district (via Kangalancheri, PIN 610101). Tiruvarur and Nagapattinam are the nearest rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
